title: Johnson: Truths, at Last
author: La Jornada Editorial Board
content:
_This editorial originally appeared in the[July 31, 2026 edition of La
Jornada](https://www.jornada.com.mx/2026/07/31/edito), Mexico's premier left
wing daily newspaper._

The United States ambassador to our country, Ronald Johnson, highlighted the
ties, the work, and the collaboration with Mexico, which have produced**
"concrete results on priority issues" such as the border, which he called "the
most secure it has ever been in its history."** He acknowledged that overdose
deaths in his country have fallen by as much as 35 percent thanks to Mexico
"carrying out historic seizures of narcotics and dismantling thousands of drug
laboratories." The security agencies of both countries, he elaborated,
continue working to share information and collaborate against transnational
criminal organizations.

**Johnson may say one thing today and change his version tomorrow, but in this
case his statements are backed by facts.** In less than two years, the number
of intentional homicides fell by 48 percent, and this past June it reached its
lowest level since 2015. In some states, the drop in lethal violence was
greater than 60 percent. Under Operation Enjambre, 60 public servants and
former public servants who provided protection to organized crime
organizations or who directly belonged to them have been arrested, regardless
of the political affiliation of the accused. Also, 56,000 people connected to
high-impact crimes have been brought to justice, among them leaders of every
faction of organized crime. More than 2,000 clandestine laboratories have been
destroyed and 420 tons of various drugs seized, as well as 30,000 firearms in
the hands of criminal structures, which in their overwhelming majority come
from the United States. By May 2026, the flow of fentanyl to the north was
reduced by 76 percent, a figure validated by the U.S. Customs and Border
Protection (CBP). It acknowledged that in April it recorded the lowest monthly
figure of seizures of that opioid at its southern border in the last four
years, as a direct consequence of the containment carried out in Mexico.

With all these figures available to Ambassador Johnson, **one must ask why he
does not inform President Trump and his cabinet about the true situation of
the fight against organized crime in Mexico, or why U.S. officials choose to
ignore reality and make statements as crude as they are false regarding the
criminal landscape in our country.** If the magnate and his team are aware of
the data recognized by their own legations and agencies, there is no
explanation for their spouting of nonsense such as the notion of an identity
between the Mexican government and the cartels, the supposed need for a
military intervention to halt the trafficking of narcotics, the control of
criminal groups over nearly the entire territory, or the characterization of
Mexico as a failed state.

In light of Johnson's admissions and the verifiable facts,**it is clear that
the slanders issued by Trumpism against Mexico are pure propaganda,** poured
over U.S. society with at least three evident purposes: to conceal the failure
of the Republican administration to solve the most pressing problems of the
population –from the rising cost of living to the grave deterioration of the
health system–,**to divert attention from the permissiveness of U.S.
authorities at all levels toward the drug-trafficking structures that operate
within their territory, and to justify Washington 's interventionist agenda
over Mexico and Latin America.**
